verification_checks.check: Expand the hbar-n coefficient of the relative QME. The terms are (S,H_n), (H_0,H_n), sum from r=1 to n of (M_r,H_n-r), one half of the internal H_r brackets, and minus Delta H_n-1.
Insert J_half=(4i)^(-N) into W_Y=T*W_X-hbar log J_half. The result is W_Y=T*W_X+hbar N log(4i).

Split the canonical BV operator into horizontal and vertical derivatives, include the raw fiber parity sign (-1)^p, integrate the vertical derivative as a total derivative, impose exactly the zero-flux equation 4E.35, and compose with odd-symplectic naturality.
Each monomial in S_ctr omits one member of every canonical base-antifield pair, so all four displayed mixed second derivatives vanish separately.
The anticommutator of two kappa-skew adjoint matrices is kappa-symmetric; transpose and cyclic trace send d_abc to minus itself, so d_abc=0 over C.

For the action truncated below order n, all lower QME-defect coefficients vanish and the order-n coefficient is minus o_n. The order-n Bianchi coefficient is therefore minus d_0 o_n, proving closedness before assigning the Hbar1 class.
Raw fiber integration has parity p_nu and degree q_nu. The graded chain identity has sign (-1)^p; an ordinary even integer-graded action is extracted only when p_nu=q_nu=0.

On the original antifield-zero Lagrangian with flat density, S_ctr restricts to zero, the exponential coefficient is one, the eta_1 eta_2 w Berezin integral of one vanishes, and noncompact even directions have no damping.
The continuum comparison is typed only after even degree-zero RG maps, a representative-level local differential, bracket limit, continuum CME, and the d_h/d_sp bicomplex identities are assumed.
Classify every pullback by coefficient type: T_nu,0^* acts on functions, T_nu,1/2^* on semidensities, T_nu,1^* on densities, and the unsubscripted geometric pullback only on differential forms.
The vertical cycle is fixed over x and x^*, so horizontal derivatives produce no moving-cycle term; BV-Stokes separately removes the vertical boundary flux on the full stable domain.

For the full-density ratio rho=exp(ell)rho_flat, expand Delta_flat exp(ell/2) exactly and obtain Delta_flat ell plus one quarter of the self bracket; this is separate from the action condition (ell,S_ctr)=0.

A Log(4i) branch shift changes W by 2 pi i hbar N and leaves the semidensity fixed. For a comparison vacuum term, N'=exp(-hbar^(n-1)zeta_n)N changes W by -hbar^n zeta_n; frozen normalization instead requires zeta_n=0.
